turns.text:
I submitted the test and job J-2219 was **not released**: no panel passed QC. Plate 2219-1 failed and has paint runs, and that's my fault. Plates 2219-2, -3 and -4 are still uncoated and ready.

**What I did**
- **Gun:** the logbook said the gun wasn't cleaned after last night's shift, so I cleaned it before spraying. The first test line on the card was lopsided. After a second cleaning it was even.
- **Measuring the paint use:** one full coat at the default settings on 2219-1 used 30 ml. It gave only 11–16 µm dry, and the corners got about 80% of what the centre got.
- **Not enough paint:** at that rate, reaching 50–80 µm takes about 120–140 ml per panel, so about 500 ml for all four. The pot held 270 ml and no more of this paint lot (26-732) arrives until Monday. Even with a perfect process, at most about two panels could have met the spec.
- **My mistake:** to bring 2219-1 up to thickness I put on one heavy, slow coat (121 mm/s). That was too much wet paint at once, and the film sagged into runs, which can't be repaired in the booth. I should have built the thickness in several lighter coats. That coat also built up unevenly: about 44 µm at the corners and 80 µm in the centre. QC recorded 2219-1 as a fail (P1–P4 42–46 µm, P5 80 µm, runs).
- **Why I stopped:** 133 ml was left, which is about four default coats. That would have put the corners of a second panel right at about 50 µm, so it would likely have failed too, and the job could not be released anyway. An uncoated plate is worth more than a failed coated one, so I kept 2219-2, -3 and -4 bare and submitted with about 10 minutes of robot time left.

**Note for the manager**
- **Paint:** J-2219 needs about 500–600 ml of ZR-2, roughly double the 270 ml that was filled. At standoff 200 mm only a small share of the sprayed paint ends up on the plate, so a fuller pot is needed, or a check on whether a shorter standoff improves that.
- **2219-1:** needs to be stripped and recoated.
- **Gun cleaning:** the gun should be cleaned at the end of every shift. The solvent ran out last night.
- **Lesson for me:** build thickness in several coats with flash-off between them, not one slow heavy coat.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.

- Paint: one pot of zinc-rich primer ZR-2; `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
